selection.method: Eight full bodies selected from the first ten completed manuscripts present at review start, including the four requested source-comparison cases.

articles.title: B106E: why the Fusion junction box can switch an output off

sourceComparison.locator: Pinpoint Test A: DTCs B106E, B106F; Normal Operation and complete pinpoint diagnostic sequence
sourceComparison.sourceRead: Complete downloaded original Ford procedure text as mirrored by Operation CHARM.
verifiedClaims: Normal Operation describes three progressive overload thresholds, with B106E and the affected circuit DTC at the first two thresholds.
The documented recovery before the third threshold requires fault correction, clearing DTCs and a self-test.
A1 explicitly requires underlying fault correction before another self-test and warns of damage to a replacement SJB.
The article distinguishes B106F permanent disablement from B106E rather than automatically prescribing module replacement.
sourceComparison.imageInspection: The inspected source HTML contains no images.
sourceComparison.result: No correction identified in the compared claims.

articles.title: B10D7: when the Fusion reports a key-programming failure

sourceComparison.locator: Pinpoint Test I: DTC B10D7:05; Normal Operation and complete pinpoint diagnostic sequence
sourceComparison.sourceRead: Complete downloaded original Ford procedure text as mirrored by Operation CHARM.
verifiedClaims: Pinpoint Test I explicitly concerns B10D7:05, PATS Key: System Programming Failures; the article preserves the suffix limitation.
Normal Operation identifies defective transponder or key-programming concern, with a PATS no-start.
I1 requires both keys individually, an additional compatible cut key when only one exists, and warns about unapproved key behavior over temperature.
The article correctly describes programming, clearing IPC DTCs, ignition cycling and checking each key without offering an anti-theft bypass.
sourceComparison.imageInspection: The inspected source HTML contains no images.
sourceComparison.result: No correction identified in the compared claims.

articles.title: C1742: why the Fusion parking aid can detect an obstacle but stay silent

sourceComparison.locator: Pinpoint Test F: DTC C1742 or DTC C1743; Normal Operation and complete pinpoint diagnostic sequence
sourceComparison.sourceRead: Complete downloaded original Ford procedure text as mirrored by Operation CHARM.
verifiedClaims: Normal Operation distinguishes C1742 open/short-to-ground sounder circuit from C1743 short-to-voltage.
F1 prioritizes other parking-aid DTCs; F2 tests the disconnected speaker for40–60ohms.
F3/F4 repeat positive-circuit grounding checks with the speaker connected then disconnected to distinguish the fault path.
F5/F6 use less than 5 ohms for the positive and negative continuity checks; F8 checks the module connection before the replacement branch.
The article does not claim a defective ultrasonic sensor from the sounder code and appropriately separates silence from obstacle clearance.
sourceComparison.imageInspection: No source images inspected. All compared numerical thresholds and branch instructions were explicit in HTML text; no diagram-specific claim was assessed.
sourceComparison.result: No correction identified in the compared claims.

articles.title: B2A25: a door-lock request that stays grounded on the Fusion

sourceComparison.locator: Pinpoint Test H: DTC B2A25, B2574, Or B2575; Normal Operation and complete pinpoint diagnostic sequence
sourceComparison.sourceRead: Complete downloaded original Ford procedure text as mirrored by Operation CHARM.
verifiedClaims: Normal Operation gives the Fusion/Milan SJB switch-input arrangement separately from the MKZ driver-door-module branch.
B2A25 is on-demand, triggered by a grounded lock/unlock request input; holding either switch longer than 2 minutes can also set it.
H2 tests the passenger switch first; H3 adds the driver switch specifically for Fusion/Milan.
H4 tests isolated request circuits against greater than 10,000 ohms before the SJB connection branch, matching the article.
The article explicitly avoids applying the MKZ driver-door-module and B2574/B2575 branch to the Fusion.
sourceComparison.imageInspection: No source images inspected. All compared numerical thresholds and branch instructions were explicit in HTML text; no diagram-specific claim was assessed.
sourceComparison.result: No correction identified in the compared claims.

limitations: This is a bounded AI editorial review of the exact recorded body/file hashes, not a full-batch or full-corpus certification.
Four additional bodies were read without separately recorded source comparisons. B106F shares the source used for B106E, but is not counted as an additional deep comparison.
The primary diagnostic text is an archived Ford workshop manual mirrored by Operation CHARM; no claim is made that it is the latest Ford service information.
No vehicle compatibility beyond each documented source scope, hands-on diagnosis, repair outcome, human mechanic certification, live deployment or search indexing was verified.
Source wiring images in C1742 and B2A25 were not inspected; comparisons relied on complete textual steps and their explicit thresholds.
Later edits require comparing the recorded hashes before extending these findings.
